TalkTalk Scam Call UK: Spot a Fake Support Call

TalkTalk says it will not use an account number to prove a call is genuine, ask for a full password, or request bank details to process a refund.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-05-23 · Updated 2026-07-19 · 3 min read

TalkTalk scam callTalkTalk phone scam UKTalkTalk impersonation
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

What a scam call looks like

A caller claims there is a broadband fault, security problem, bill issue or refund. They may ask for remote access to a computer, send the victim to a website, request a full password or bank details, or demand payment through a hard-to-trace service.

TalkTalk genuinely contacts customers, so the topic of a call does not authenticate it. Caller ID can be spoofed, and an account number may have been obtained elsewhere.

TalkTalk's published “never” rules

TalkTalk says it will not:

  • use the TalkTalk account number to prove the call is genuine;
  • ask for the full password — it says it asks for only two digits;
  • ask for bank details to process a refund; or
  • ask for money through MoneyGram or Western Union.

Its current guidance also describes automated “press 1” engineer calls claiming to be TalkTalk as a scam pattern.

Warning signs

  • A request to install or open remote-access software.
  • A demand for the full password or for bank details to issue a refund.
  • The account number is offered as proof of identity.
  • The caller insists you stay on the line while banking or making a payment.
  • An automated message asks you to press 1 for an engineer.

Check the call safely

Hang up and call TalkTalk using the number on a bill or its official website. TalkTalk says customers can dial 150 from a TalkTalk home phone. If a bank is mentioned, hang up and use the bank's trusted number or 159 if the bank participates.

TalkTalk CallSafe

CallSafe costs £1 a month from 11 January 2026. It can be added or managed in My Account where compatible. TalkTalk says that after a withheld-number call, dialling 1472 lets a CallSafe user block or approve that caller. The separate 1471 caller-return service does not activate CallSafe.

CallSafe screens some unknown callers by asking them to record their name, but it does not make every call safe and compatibility requirements apply.

If remote access or details were given

Disconnect the affected device from the internet if the caller may still have access. Contact the bank immediately where financial information or payment is involved. From a different trusted device, change relevant passwords and review accounts. TalkTalk advises having affected devices checked for viruses, spyware and adware; a factory reset should not be stated as routinely necessary without technical assessment.

Reporting in the UK

Report related phishing emails to TalkTalk at phishing@talktalk.co.uk and to the NCSC at report@phishing.gov.uk. If money was lost or an account or device was compromised, report the crime to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland; in Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101.

Frequently asked questions

Is CallSafe free?

No. TalkTalk says the price increased to £1 a month from 11 January 2026.

Does dialling 1471 activate CallSafe?

No. Add or manage CallSafe through My Account where available. TalkTalk describes 1472 specifically for blocking or approving a withheld caller after that call.
